program_name: Professional Bachelor in Wood Technology (German: Berufsbildender Bachelor in Holztechnik; Italian: Laurea professionalizzante in Tecnologie del Legno). unibz also renders the German name as 'Professioneller Bachelor in Holztechnologie' in the EN page metadata, so two German variants circulate. Faculty of Engineering. Degree Course Director: Prof. Francesco Patuzzi. Student representative in the Course Council: Sebastiano Marchesoni. STATUS: SUSPENDED - no intake in 2026/27.
level: bachelor (professional bachelor / laurea a orientamento professionale / berufsbildender Bachelor). 180 ECTS over 3 years. This is Italy's 'professionalising' bachelor type, distinguished by a compulsory 50 ECTS of in-company placement out of 180.
teaching_language: Trilingual (German / Italian / English), with no single dominant language and NO English-only pathway. Brochure verbatim: 'Unterrichtssprachen: Deutsch, Italienisch und Englisch (Studium in allen drei Sprachen)'; Italian brochure: 'Lingue di insegnamento: italiano, tedesco e inglese (si studia in tutte e tre le lingue)'. Actual per-course language codes from the official Course Offering page (cohort 'Enrolled from 2022', academic year 2025/26 - the last year with a complete three-year listing, checked 2026-08-29): roughly 17 course units in English, 10 in Italian and 9 in German. English is the largest single language but is NOT sufficient, because compulsory core courses are locked to one language with no English alternative. German-only compulsory courses: Wood Chemistry (+ its laboratory), Physics, Mechanics of Structures (+ laboratory), Mechatronics and Process Automation, High-Performance Buildings: Seismic Design and Fire Resistance (+ laboratory). Italian-only compulsory courses: Wood Anatomy and Productive Forestry (+ laboratory), Product Design (+ laboratory), Economy, Law, Contracts, Construction Site 4.0 (+ laboratory), Operational Safety and LCA Evaluation (+ laboratory). English-taught core: Mathematics (+ laboratory), Heat and Mass Transfer (+ laboratory), Material Sciences (+ laboratory), Energy Efficiency in Wood Production and Final Use (+ laboratory), Fundamentals of Programming (+ laboratory), Technical Drawing - CAD (+ laboratory), High-Performance Buildings: Comfort and Energy Efficiency (+ laboratory), Laboratory of Physics applied to Mechanics. A 3 CP 'Specialised Language' slot exists in all three languages (Italian / German / English) and the student takes one. The bilingual course-content PDF corroborates this: syllabus text is written in English for some courses, in German for Physics and Heat and Mass Transfer, and in Italian for Wood Anatomy and Product Design. Note the unibz disclaimer on the source listing: 'On this page we show the lectures that are currently offered in the two semesters. It does not illustrate the structure of the study programme.' [uncertain]
campus: NOI Techpark Bozen-Bolzano (NOI Techpark, Bruno-Buozzi-Strasse 1 / via Bruno Buozzi 1, 39100 Bozen-Bolzano) - the Faculty of Engineering's technology-park campus, NOT the Universitaetsplatz main campus and NOT Brixen-Bressanone, Bruneck-Brunico, Trento or Innsbruck. All three language versions of the programme page agree ('Campus: NOI Techpark Bozen' / 'Campus: NOI Techpark Bolzano'). This corrects the working assumption of a generic 'Bolzano' campus in the research outline. Historically the programme sat on the plain Bolzano campus of the former Faculty of Science and Technology (2019/20 Study Manifesto: 'Facolta: Scienze e Tecnologie (campus di Bolzano)') before the 2023 faculty reorganisation moved it to Engineering at NOI Techpark. In addition, at least 50 of the 180 ECTS are earned off campus, in companies and technical offices.
degree_class: L-P03 (Professioni tecniche industriali e dell'informazione / Industrial and Information Technical Professions), one of the Italian 'lauree professionalizzanti' classes. 180 ECTS, 3 years. Verbatim from all three brochures: 'Bachelorklasse: L-P03' / 'Classe di laurea: L-P03'. IMPORTANT HISTORICAL CHANGE: the programme did not start in L-P03. Its 2019/20 founding Study Manifesto places it in class L-9 (Ingegneria industriale) under the name 'Corso di laurea a orientamento professionale in Ingegneria del Legno': 'Classe delle lauree L-9'. The move from L-9 to L-P03 accompanied the rename from Wood Engineering to Wood Technology. The degree gives access to the professional register of 'Perito industriale'; under the current L-P03 regime this is possible WITHOUT the State Examination, whereas the 2019/20 L-9 version still required it ('l'accesso all'Albo degli Periti industriali previo superamento dell'esame di stato').
offered_in_2026_27: NO - NOT OFFERED. The programme is suspended for 2026/27 and must be recorded in any dataset as unavailable to new applicants. unibz states this explicitly and identically in all three languages, inside the 'Course description' block at the top of the programme page and reproduced in the brochures: EN 'This study programme will not be offered in the 2026/27 academic year.'; DE 'Dieser Studiengang wird im akademischen Jahr 2026/27 nicht angeboten.'; IT 'Questo corso di laurea non sara attivato nell'anno accademico 2026/27.' Five independent confirmations were obtained on 2026-08-29: (1) the explicit notice in EN/DE/IT; (2) the entire 'Application and Admission' section - deadlines, available places, entry requirements, language requirements, admission procedure, tuition - has been REMOVED from the live programme page, whereas the archived 2025/26 and 2024/25 versions of the same page carried it in full; (3) the admission-information PDF, in both English and German, is now an empty shell containing only the Advisory Service contact block and the footer 'Latest update: 21.05.2026' - no deadlines, no places, no requirements; (4) the programme appears in NONE of the published 2026/27 ranking lists (the Engineering faculty lists only Computer Science, Electronic and Information Engineering, Industrial and Mechanical Engineering, and Informatics and Management of Digital Business); (5) the programme is absent from the 2026/27 Additional Application Session (18 August - 4 September 2026), which lists the same four Engineering bachelors. The LAST INTAKE was academic year 2025/26. THE PROGRAMME IS NOT CLOSED, ONLY CLOSED TO NEW ENTRANTS: teaching continues for already-enrolled students, and the official Course Offering page still schedules 19 course units for 2026/27 (second- and third-year subjects only - every first-year course such as Mathematics, Wood Chemistry, Wood Anatomy, Product Design, Physics, Fundamentals of Programming, Technical Drawing and Economy/Law/Contracts has disappeared from the 2026/27 listing, which is exactly the signature of a teach-out). A 2027/28 tab exists on that page but currently lists no courses. DATA TRAP: the programme is still listed as a normal bachelor in the Engineering faculty navigation menu alongside active programmes, the page still carries the stale recruitment string 'Courses will definetely be starting' (unibz's own typo), and both brochure PDFs are still downloadable and still show places, fees and a full study plan - so any scraper that keys off the menu, the brochure or the PDF's existence will wrongly mark this programme as open.
is_new_programme: No - the opposite. This is a discontinuing programme, not a new one, and it is one of the shortest-lived degrees unibz has run: launched in 2019/20 and closed to new entrants after 2025/26, i.e. roughly seven intakes. Documented lineage: (a) 2019/20 - founded as 'Corso di laurea a orientamento professionale in Ingegneria del Legno' (Professional Bachelor in Wood Engineering), degree class L-9, Faculty of Science and Technology, Bolzano campus, 20 EU places, THREE curricula (Industriale, Edile del Legno, Alto Artigianato), annual fees EUR 1,347.50, selection by school-record evaluation plus entrance test, register access only after the State Examination; (b) subsequently reclassified into the new professionalising class L-P03 and renamed Wood Technology / Tecnologie del Legno / Holztechnik, with the three curricula consolidated into TWO majors and direct register access without the State Examination; (c) moved to the Faculty of Engineering at NOI Techpark in the March 2023 faculty reorganisation that split the former Faculty of Science and Technology (the legacy URL /de/faculties/sciencetechnology/bachelor-wood-technology/ still appears in search indexes); (d) last intake 2025/26; (e) suspended from 2026/27. The exact academic year of the L-9 to L-P03 reclassification and rename is not stated on any unibz page located during this verification, and no unibz decree, news item or press release explaining or announcing the suspension was found. [uncertain]
majors_tracks_study_plans: TWO majors (called 'branches of study' / 'curricula' by unibz), diverging from the second year on a common first year. Programme page verbatim: 'In the first year, students will deepen their knowledge of basic subjects such as mathematics, wood anatomy, silviculture, product design and materials science. From the second year onwards, the programme is divided into two branches of study'. (1) MAJOR INDUSTRIAL AND SKILLED ARTISANSHIP - year 2: Heat and Mass Transfer, Material Sciences, Industrial Production Organization and Management, Electronics/Diagnosis and Quality Control; year 3: Manufacturing Technology, Energy Efficiency in Wood Production and Final Use, Mechatronics and Process Automation, Industrial Plants and Logistics, Final Exam (3 CP). (2) MAJOR WOODEN BUILDINGS - year 2: Heat and Mass Transfer, Material Sciences, Construction Site 4.0, Mechanics of Structures; year 3: Energy Efficiency in Wood Production and Final Use, High-Performance Buildings: Comfort and Energy Efficiency, High-Performance Buildings: Seismic Design and Fire Resistance, Mechatronics and Process Automation, Operational Safety and LCA, Evaluation Final Exam (3 CP). Shared first year (both majors): Mathematics 6, Fundamentals of Information Science and Microcontroller Programming 6, Economy/Law/Contracts 6, Wood Chemistry 6, Physics 6, Wood Anatomy and Productive Forestry 6, Product Design 10, Fundamentals of Programming 6, Technical Drawing - CAD 6, Specialised Language 3 CP. The Industrial major additionally offers a first-year complementary choice between 'Logging, sawmill operations and traceability procedures of wood' (6 CP) and 'Economics of Family Businesses' (6 CP). Common to both majors from year 2: 12 ECTS of optional/free-choice courses and 50 ECTS of internship ('Stage 1' 25 CP + 'Stage 2' 25 CP). Free-choice credits may be taken from the Bachelor in Industrial and Mechanical Engineering without Course Council approval, from other Faculty of Engineering bachelors with prior approval, or elsewhere with prior approval. There is no dual-study variant and no part-time plan. Note the predecessor L-9 programme had THREE curricula (Industriale, Edile del Legno, Alto Artigianato); the current two majors merge the industrial and high-craft strands.
english_only_accessibility: effectively-closed - and now closed outright. Two independent barriers apply. FIRST AND DECISIVE for 2026/27: the programme accepts no applications at all, so it is unavailable to every candidate regardless of language. SECOND, structural, and the reason it would still have been closed to an English-only candidate in any prior cycle: admission required B2 in the FIRST language AND B2 in the SECOND language chosen from German, Italian and English, so English alone filled only one of the two mandatory slots and a second B2 in German or Italian was compulsory - 'The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English. Therefore, the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure'. The 2019/20 founding manifesto set the same bar from the start: 'Livello B2 in almeno 2 lingue di insegnamento'. Even a candidate who cleared entry could not complete the degree in English: five compulsory course units are German-only (Wood Chemistry, Physics, Mechanics of Structures, Mechatronics and Process Automation, High-Performance Buildings: Seismic Design and Fire Resistance) and five are Italian-only (Wood Anatomy and Productive Forestry, Product Design, Economy/Law/Contracts, Construction Site 4.0, Operational Safety and LCA), each with matching laboratories in the same language. Graduation additionally demanded C1 / C1 / B2 across all three languages. Finally, the compulsory 50 ECTS internship is served in South Tyrolean wood-industry companies and technical offices, where German and Italian are the working languages in practice. For a Turkish applicant holding only English, this programme should be presented as unavailable - permanently for 2026/27, and structurally even if it were to be reactivated.
admission_type: NOT APPLICABLE FOR 2026/27 - there is no admission procedure, no application window and no ranking list, because the programme is not activated. For historical reference, the regime in force through the final 2025/26 intake was: restricted access (numerus clausus) with a compulsory ONLINE ENTRANCE EXAMINATION. Verbatim from the 2025/26 programme page: 'In addition to language skills and formal requirements, access to the degree programme is through a selection process. Admission Exam (max. 100 points): A multiple choice test will give information about the prior knowledge of the applicants in the field of logic, mathematics and science subjects.' No TOLC-I, no CENT-S, no SAT, no portfolio and no interview were used - unibz ran its own test. A language pre-check (B2 in two of the three teaching languages) acted as a hard filter before ranking. In the 2024/25 cycle the same test was scored out of 60 points, so the rubric was rescaled to 100 for the final 2025/26 cycle. The original 2019/20 programme combined a school-record evaluation with the entrance test ('Procedura di selezione: Valutazione del rendimento scolastico e test d'ingresso'); by the final cycles the published procedure was the test alone.
academic_requirements: NOT APPLICABLE FOR 2026/27 (no intake). Historical requirements as published for the final 2025/26 intake: 'To gain admission to the programme you need one of the following qualifications: a secondary school leaving certificate (Italian system); equivalent qualification obtained abroad. Foreign school leaving certificates are considered equivalent if obtained after 12 years of education. In this case, you furthermore must have attended at least the last two years in the foreign school system (e.g. Irish Leaving Certificate: it is not enough to attend one year and obtain the foreign certificate).' The Italian Ministry of Education, University and Research imposed extra requirements on holders of certain certificates, explicitly naming American high school diplomas and British and Greek certificates, with candidates directed to apply@unibz.it (Advisory Service). Language requirements had to be met or the candidate was excluded from the procedure. National rule on parallel enrolment: 'According to national regulations, simultaneous enrolment in a maximum of 2 programmes is possible (however, the two programmes must not belong to the same class, e.g., L-18/L-18 and must differ for at least 2/3 of the course contents).' Subject knowledge in logic, mathematics and science subjects was tested by the entrance exam rather than required as a prerequisite. No ECTS or SSD credit prerequisites applied - that regime concerns master programmes. A Turkish 'Lise Diplomasi' satisfies the 12-year rule but would have needed ARDI/CIMEA documentation (see credential_recognition).
entry_exam_or_test: NOT APPLICABLE FOR 2026/27 - no exam is scheduled and no exam dates are published, because there is no admission round. Historical detail, final 2025/26 intake: a single unibz-run ONLINE MULTIPLE-CHOICE admission test covering logic, mathematics and science subjects, worth a maximum of 100 points, offered on two dates - 2025-05-14 at 15:00 local time (Early Bird) and 2025-07-17 at 15:00 local time (Late Application). 'The result of the admission test in one of these dates remains valid for the admission procedure of the current academic year.' unibz published a downloadable specimen paper ('Here you can find an example of the admission exam'). In the 2024/25 cycle the equivalent test was held on 2024-05-14 at 15:00 and scored out of 60 points. The programme never accepted TOLC-I or CENT-S, unlike the unibz engineering bachelors that continue. Separately, and not an admission test, unibz Language Centre B2 exams could be used to prove language proficiency; in the 2025/26 cycle these ran on 2025-03-17 (registration 2025-03-03 to 2025-03-09), on 16-17 and 22-23 April (registration 2025-03-24 to 2025-04-08 - unibz's own page misprinted the April dates with the year 2024), and 2025-06-23 to 2025-06-27 for the Late session (registration 2025-05-28 to 2025-06-15).
selection_scoring: NOT APPLICABLE FOR 2026/27. Historical: the final published rubric was a single component - 'Admission Exam (max. 100 points)' - a multiple-choice test on logic, mathematics and science subjects, with the ranking built on that score. unibz did NOT publish a minimum pass mark, a cut-off score or a minimum grade point average for this programme, and because no 2025/26 or 2024/25 ranking list for Wood Technology could be located in the public ranking-list archive, no admitted-score floor can be reported either. This contrasts with programmes where thresholds are published (Design 42/100, Critical Creative Practices 60/100, EMMA 55/95, Entrepreneurship 70/100) and with masters carrying grade minimums (Software Engineering 24/30, Energy Engineering 22/30). The only score-linked consequence documented is the OFA trigger: 'If on the day of the exam the Admission Committee evaluates your prior knowledge as inadequate, you may be assigned additional learning obligations' - the inadequacy threshold itself is not quantified. The 2024/25 cycle used a 60-point scale for the same test, confirming the rubric was rescaled at least once. The 2019/20 predecessor also weighted school records alongside the test, a component absent from the final published procedure. [uncertain]
bonus_points: None documented. No Webometrics university-ranking bonus (that applies to the Master in Software Engineering and the Master in Computing for Data Science), no GMAT/GRE bonus (Master in Accounting and Finance), no start-up project bonus (Master in Entrepreneurship and Innovation), and no published bonus for vocational or wood-sector background, apprenticeship, work experience, competitions or South Tyrolean residence - which is notable given the programme's strong vocational and local-industry orientation. The published selection procedure for the final 2025/26 intake consisted solely of the 100-point admission exam, with no additive components and no tie-break rule stated. The absence is inferred from the archived programme page and the empty admission-information PDF rather than from an explicit statement that no bonuses exist, and no ranking list survives to cross-check whether a tie-break or bonus was applied in practice. [uncertain]
portfolio_and_materials: None required. No portfolio, no video, no project proposal, no motivation letter, no CV and no reference letters were requested at any point - unlike Design and Art, Critical Creative Practices or Eco-Social Design. The format limits published for those programmes (portfolio max 20 MB PDF, project proposal max 2 A4 pages, motivation letter max 6,000 characters, video max 2 minutes) never applied here. Selection rested entirely on the multiple-choice admission exam. What had to be uploaded to the application portal was purely administrative: a valid ID card or passport scanned front and back ('if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure'), the completed online form with attachments, the secondary school diploma where already held, and language evidence. For 2026/27 nothing at all can be submitted, since the programme accepts no applications.
interview: No interview, in any cycle. Selection was decided by the written multiple-choice admission exam alone; the Admission Committee evaluated only material uploaded to the portal by the deadline plus the test result. Verbatim: 'The Admission Committee will only evaluate the documents uploaded in the portal by the application deadline.' No interview dates were ever published for this programme, in contrast to, for example, the Master in Computing for Data Science, which schedules interviews for below-threshold candidates. For 2026/27 the question is moot - there is no selection process to interview for.
conditional_admission: NOT APPLICABLE FOR 2026/27. Historical: applicants who had not yet obtained their secondary school diploma could apply - 'If you gained your qualification abroad, you must also upload the diploma of your qualification: if you are not yet in possession of the diploma, you'll need to upload it upon enrolment.' Admission remained provisional until unibz validated the foreign qualification, and 'if you do not possess a valid admission qualification, you can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment.' Financial protection mirrored the general unibz rule: the first instalment was refundable only where the candidate failed the secondary school final exam or, for non-EU applicants living abroad, could not obtain the documents needed for enrolment from the Italian authorities. There was NO ECTS-based conditional admission (the 120 ECTS / 140 ECTS rule applies to master programmes only), and no late-enrolment window comparable to the 11/12/2026 date used elsewhere was published for this bachelor. Because the admission-information PDF is now empty and only the archived page survives, this description is reconstructed from the last active cycle plus unibz's general enrolment rules rather than from a current programme-specific source. [uncertain]
ofa_rules: OFA (obblighi formativi aggiuntivi / additional learning obligations) applied and were triggered by the ENTRANCE EXAM result, not by school grades - the opposite of the Bachelor in Sustainable Agriculture and Forestry, and different again from the mandatory-maths-test OFA used by Economics and Management, Economics Politics and Ethics and Tourism Sport and Event Management. Verbatim from the final 2025/26 cycle: 'If on the day of the exam the Admission Committee evaluates your prior knowledge as inadequate, you may be assigned additional learning obligations to be achieved by the end of the first academic year.' Remediation: 'preparatory courses are offered in the weeks before the beginning of the first semester. In particular, the courses are taught as intensive courses in which the basic concepts of mathematics, physics, biology and chemistry are dealt with. The additional educational debt is absolved by passing a special examination.' The Study Guide adds that OFA for this programme are assigned 'in the mathematics or physics area', that a catch-up course runs before the first semester, and that the obligation can alternatively be cleared by passing the 'Analisi I' or 'Physik I' exam within the first year. CONSEQUENCE OF FAILURE - and this is harsher than at most unibz bachelors: 'The OFA-exam must be passed within the first academic year of study and is an essential prerequisite for taking the curricular exams of the years following the first. If you have not passed the OFA exam in one of the sessions planned, you will be not able to enrol in the second year of study; consequently, you will be enrolled in the first year again.' At the agriculture and engineering bachelors a student with unfulfilled OFA may still enrol in year 2 (merely barred from year 2 and 3 exams); here the student is held back and re-enrolled in year 1. Mathematics and Physics pre-courses ran 2025-09-22 to 2025-10-03 in the final cycle. No OFA can be assigned in 2026/27 since there is no intake.
language_requirements: Trilingual regime with a hard two-language entry bar - historically binding, now moot for applicants but still binding on enrolled students who must graduate. Entry (final 2025/26 intake): B2 in the first language AND B2 in the second language, no level required in the third. Verbatim: 'The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English. Therefore, the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure.' Exit (to graduate): C1 first language, C1 second language, B2 third language - the Study Guide is blunt about the consequence: 'If you are not able to certify these levels you are not allowed to graduate.' Position, not identity, defines the level: 'Your first language is the language in which you have the highest level of proficiency (B2 or C1). Your third language is instead the language in which you are weaker (or in which you are an absolute beginner).' Certification was mandatory for the first and second language and recommended from B1 upwards for the third. B1 in the third language is the minimum for sitting curricular exams held in that language. Language Centre courses are free of charge, targeting B1 in the third language by the end of year 1 and B2 by the end of year 2, delivered as extensive courses of 4 hours per week during semesters and intensive courses of 6 hours per day between semesters; absolute beginners must use the September intensive session because 'Beginner courses (A1) will be offered exclusively during the pre-semester intensive course session in September will no longer be offered during the academic year.' Admitted students who could not certify the third language sat a placement test and were assigned a learning path toward B2. The two-language B2 bar dates back to the programme's foundation: the 2019/20 manifesto already recorded 'Requisiti linguistici: Livello B2 in almeno 2 lingue di insegnamento'. Because the curriculum genuinely splits across all three languages, the third language was never peripheral here - a student meets German-only and Italian-only compulsory courses from the first year onward.
entry_levels_by_position: 1st language B2 / 2nd language B2 / 3rd language no level required at entry. Levels attach to POSITION, not to a specific language: the applicant assigns German, Italian and English to the three slots according to the levels actually certified, the first language being the strongest. This places Wood Technology in the stricter B2/B2 tier - the same as the Bachelor in Computer Science and the full-time engineering study plans, and above the Bachelor in Electronic and Information Engineering (B2/B1) - and unlike Industrial and Mechanical Engineering there was no dual-study variant offering a relaxed B2/B1 entry. Two operational riders applied: 'A B1 level in the third language is the minimum requirement for taking curricular examinations in that specific language', and 'if the first semester of your study programme is only taught in English and your third language is English, you will have to certify at least a B1 level in English by mid-January to be able to take all the curricular exams scheduled for the first semester.' The unibz Language Centre could only certify at one level - 'Please note that you can only register for B2 level exams' - so that route could fill a second-language slot but could never by itself produce the C1 needed for graduation. For 2026/27 these entry levels are inoperative, no candidate being admitted; the exit levels below remain live for the teach-out cohorts.
exit_levels: 1st language C1, 2nd language C1, 3rd language B2 - graduation requirements, not admission requirements, and they remain fully in force for the students still completing the programme during the teach-out. A student admitted at B2/B2 therefore had to raise both languages to C1 and additionally reach B2 in the third language before graduating. The Study Guide states the sanction directly: 'To be admitted to the degree examination you must certify the following minimum levels in the three languages: 1st language: C1, 2nd language: C1, 3rd language: B2. If you are not able to certify these levels you are not allowed to graduate.' Free Language Centre provision supports this, with intermediate third-language milestones of B1 by the end of year 1 and B2 by the end of year 2 - meaning the third-language exit level is expected a full year before graduation. For a student who entered with, say, English C1 and Italian B2, the practical workload was Italian to C1 plus German from scratch to B2 within three years, on top of a curriculum already carrying 50 ECTS of in-company placement.
third_language_exam_threshold: B1 in the third language is the threshold for taking curricular examinations delivered in that language. Verbatim: 'A B1 level in the third language is the minimum requirement for taking curricular examinations in that specific language.' Special case: 'Please note that if the first semester of your study programme is only taught in English and your third language is English, you will have to certify at least a B1 level in English by mid-January to be able to take all the curricular exams scheduled for the first semester.' This rule bites unusually hard in Wood Technology because the compulsory curriculum is genuinely distributed across all three languages from year 1 - a student whose third language is German cannot sit Wood Chemistry, Physics, Mechanics of Structures, Mechatronics or High-Performance Buildings: Seismic Design without B1 German, and a student whose third language is Italian is blocked from Wood Anatomy, Product Design, Economy/Law/Contracts, Construction Site 4.0 and Operational Safety/LCA. Students unable to certify the third language took a placement test after admission and were assigned a learning path toward B2 as soon as possible; absolute beginners were directed to the three-week September intensive course, since A1 courses run only in that pre-semester session.
proof_pathways: NOT APPLICABLE FOR 2026/27 for admission purposes (no application can be made); still relevant to enrolled students proving exit levels. Four accepted routes applied in the final 2025/26 cycle. (1) The main teaching language of the final high school year, if German, Italian or English - recognised as C1 (Ladin upper secondary schools: recognised as B2 in German and Italian); for foreign qualifications, 'If the main teaching language is not clearly stated on your hign school diploma, please also upload a letter/document issued by your high school stating the medium of instruction' (unibz's own typo). (2) A bachelor or master degree taught in Italian, German or English - recognised as C1; unibz graduates upload certificates or declare Language Centre exams passed (B2, B2+ or C1); foreign degrees need a university letter stating the medium of instruction if not shown on the diploma. (3) A recognised language certificate from the official unibz list; 'If you cannot upload the certificates, you can send them by e-mail as PDF files or deliver them in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline.' (4) A language exam organised by the unibz Language Centre, booked through the application portal under 'enrol for language exams' after creating an application - 'Please note that you can only register for B2 level exams.' Additional route for bilingual/multilingual and foreign secondary schools: 'If the foreign language proficiency levels (for German, Italian, or English) are explicitly indicated on the diploma of graduation according to the Common European Framework of Reference (i.e., B1, B2 or C1), and if all four language abilities (reading, listening, speaking, writing) have been assessed, then the indicated levels will be accepted as a proof of proficiency for the second and/or third language', subject to Language Centre approval. Certificates from Italian public institutions required a self-declaration; those from foreign public institutions required a scanned copy of the original. Final-cycle Language Centre exam dates (2025/26 intake): 2025-03-17 (registration 2025-03-03 to 2025-03-09); 16-17 and 22-23 April 2025 (registration 2025-03-24 to 2025-04-08); 2025-06-23 to 2025-06-27 (registration 2025-05-28 to 2025-06-15).
certificate_rules: The general unibz certificate regime applied; nothing programme-specific was ever published for Wood Technology, and because the admission-information PDF is now empty there is no current programme-level source to cite. Under the university-wide rules (Resolution of the University Council governing recognised language certificates and diplomas, most recently n. 16/2026, superseding 20/2025): a certificate must assess all four skills and be issued by the certification organisation itself; where no overall level is stated, the LOWEST sub-skill level determines the certified level, provided that part was passed; there is no compensation for failed parts and no averaging unless the awarding body supplies it; certificates combining single skills from different organisations are refused; certificates of participation, end-of-course tests, private-institution exams, placement-test results and certificates issued by individual lecturers are refused; DAAD certificates are not recognised; online 'home edition' exams are not recognised except for the specific entries footnoted as such in the official list. Validity: international language certificates must not be older than five years at submission, with the whole calendar year counting from 1 January; items under 'Further Recognised Degrees, Diplomas and Certificates' have unlimited validity. Recognised providers include Goethe-Institut and OeSD for German and the corresponding boards for Italian and English, level by level from A2 to C2. Official list: https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Languages/unibz-recognised-language-certificates-v2.pdf . This paragraph reproduces the university-wide regime rather than a source verified against this suspended programme in the present check. [uncertain]
application_deadline_eu: NONE FOR 2026/27 - there is no Early Bird session, no Late Application session and no Additional Application Session for this programme, and no application can be submitted in any window. The programme is absent from the 2026/27 Additional Application Session (18 August - 4 September 2026), which for the Faculty of Engineering lists only Computer Science, Electronic and Information Engineering, Industrial and Mechanical Engineering, and Informatics and Management of Digital Business. For historical reference, the final 2025/26 intake ran two EU sessions, both closing at 12:00 noon local time: Early Bird 2025-03-03 to 2025-05-06, and Late Application (EU only) 2025-05-28 to 2025-07-09, with an Additional Session possible in August or September if places remained ('The faculty can open additional application sessions for single study programmes in August and in September if there are available places'). The 2024/25 cycle before it ran 2024-03-01 to 2024-05-07 and 2024-05-29 to 2024-07-10. unibz writes these as DD/MM/YYYY ('03/03 - 06/05/2025'), normalised to ISO here. Standard rules that applied: 'You might apply for more than one study programme. If you are excluded in the first session, you might apply again in the second one', and 'Once the application has been sent, it cannot be modified. Filled-in forms which have not been sent correctly will not be taken into consideration.'
application_deadline_non_eu: NONE FOR 2026/27 - non-EU citizens living abroad have no application route to this programme, the single window that existed in prior cycles having been withdrawn along with the whole admission procedure. Historically, non-EU citizens resident abroad had exactly one opportunity per cycle, the Early Bird window only: 2025-03-03 to 2025-05-06 (12:00 noon local time) for the final 2025/26 intake, and 2024-03-01 to 2024-05-07 for 2024/25. Verbatim: 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore. Application fee: EUR 50. The fee is an administration fee and is non-refundable.' Non-EU applicants living abroad were excluded from the Late Application and from any Additional Session, both EU-only. Practical note for Turkish applicants resident in Turkey, now historical: only 2 non-EU places existed in the entire cycle, the B2+B2 two-language proof had to be in hand by the early-May deadline, and the June Language Centre exam window fell after that deadline and was therefore useless to this group. No 2025/26 or 2024/25 ranking list for the programme could be located, so it is not possible to report whether any non-EU applicant was ever admitted.
parity_of_treatment: The standard unibz rule applied while the programme was recruiting, and is recorded here for completeness even though no application route now exists. Two categories were treated as EU citizens. (1) 'Citizens from Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino and the Vatican City State'. (2) 'Non-EU citizens with a valid permit to stay in Italy (see article 39, paragraph 5 of decree no. 286 of 25.07.1998: "permesso di soggiorno" (residence permit) for work, family reasons, political or humanitarian asylum, religious reasons). In this case, you apply directly to the University as described above and must submit a copy of your valid permit to stay. A permit to stay for study reasons or a visa for tourism is not sufficient. If the permit has expired, you must attach a renewal request.' Critical warning: 'Please note that if you do not upload the permit in the application portal, you will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad and therefore subject to the admission procedure through the Italian authorities in your country of origin.' This third category was the decisive one for Turkish nationals already living in Italy on a work, family or humanitarian permit: it opened the 20-place EU pool and both EU sessions instead of the 2-place non-EU quota, and removed the EUR 50 fee and the Universitaly/visa route. For 2026/27 the distinction has no effect on this programme - neither pool exists.
places_quotas: ZERO PLACES IN 2026/27 - none for EU citizens, none for persons given parity of treatment, none for non-EU citizens living abroad. The programme is not activated, so no quota was set and no ranking list was drawn up. Historical quotas, stable across the final cycles at 20 EU + 2 non-EU: for the 2025/26 intake the programme page listed (under an untranslated Italian heading 'Posti di studio' on the English page) 'Cittadin* UE ed equiparat*: I sessione 15, II sessione 5' and 'Cittadin* non-UE (residenti all'estero): I sessione 2'; the 2024/25 page gave the same split in English - 'Early Bird Application: 15, Late Application: 5' for EU and 'Early Bird Application: 2' for non-EU. Both brochures still advertise 'Studienplätze: 20 EU + 2 nicht-EU' / 'Posti disponibili: 20 UE + 2 non UE', which is a trap: those PDFs remain downloadable from the live page and describe a cycle that no longer exists. Unfilled Early Bird places rolled into the Late session under the usual rule ('any remaining places of the early bird application, will be offered in the late application'). The 2019/20 founding manifesto listed '20 EU' with no non-EU quota at all, so the non-EU allocation of 2 was added later. This was one of the smallest intakes at unibz, which is consistent with the decision to suspend it.
ranking_and_enrolment_dates: NOT APPLICABLE FOR 2026/27 - no ranking list will be published, no first-instalment deadline exists and no enrolment window is open for this programme; it appears in none of the 2026/27 ranking lists (Early Bird, Late or Additional Session). Historical, final 2025/26 intake: Early Bird - ranking list published by 2025-05-27, first instalment of tuition fees by 2025-06-05 12:00 noon, enrolment 2025-07-11 to 2025-08-05 12:00 noon. Late Application - ranking list by 2025-07-29, first instalment by 2025-08-05 12:00 noon, enrolment from publication of the ranking list until 2025-08-05 12:00 noon. Standard rules that applied: missing either the payment or the enrolment deadline meant automatic loss of the place ('If you do not meet this deadline, you will automatically be excluded and the next applicant in the ranking list will be admitted'); a candidate admitted to more than one programme could secure a maximum of 2 by paying the instalment twice; 'Paying university fees does not confer student status, which is only obtained by enrolling'; enrolling early was advised so that incomplete documents could be corrected before the deadline; students transferring from another Italian university had to give the Student Office a copy of the transfer application at the start of the academic year; and ranking lists 'are only valid for the respective academic year'. Note that requests to TRANSFER INTO another unibz programme follow the same calendar - 'requests for transfer to another study course at unibz follow the same deadlines as the applications of prospective students' - which is the relevant deadline for any Wood Technology student now switching out.
programme_specific_dates: NO PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC ADMISSION DATES EXIST FOR 2026/27: no admission exam, no interview, no portfolio deadline, no application window and no ranking date, because the programme is not activated. The only dates that remain live for this programme are TEACHING dates for the students being taught out. Course Offering for 2026/27 (cohort 'Enrolled from 2022') schedules 19 course units, all second- and third-year subjects, overwhelmingly in Semester 1: Laboratory of Mechatronics and Process Automation (EN), Construction Site 4.0 and its laboratory (IT), Mechanics of Structures and its laboratory (DE), Operational Safety and LCA Evaluation and its laboratory (IT), High-Performance Buildings: Comfort and Energy Efficiency and its laboratory (EN), High-Performance Buildings: Seismic Design and Fire Resistance and its laboratory (DE), Material Sciences and its laboratory (EN), Heat and Mass Transfer and its laboratory (EN), Energy Efficiency in Wood Production and Final Use and its laboratory (EN), Mechatronics and Process Automation (DE), plus the year-long 0 CP 'Elements for the exercise of the profession of "Perito Industriale" with evaluative practical test' held by Prof. Francesco Patuzzi. No first-year courses appear, confirming the teach-out. A 2027/28 tab exists on the Course Offering page but currently lists no courses. Historical programme-specific dates from the final 2025/26 intake, for reference: admission exams 2025-05-14 and 2025-07-17, both at 15:00 local time; intensive language courses 2025-09-01 to 2025-09-19 (Monday to Friday, 6 h/day); Mathematics pre-course and Physics pre-course both 2025-09-22 to 2025-10-03; Freshers Days 2025-09-29 and 2025-09-30; semester 1 classes 2025-09-29 to 2025-12-23, holidays 2025-12-24 to 2026-01-06, classes 2026-01-07 to 2026-01-24, exams 2026-01-26 to 2026-02-21; semester 2 classes 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-02, holidays 2026-04-03 to 2026-04-06, classes 2026-04-07 to 2026-06-13, exams 2026-06-15 to 2026-07-11; autumn exam session 2026-08-24 to 2026-09-26.
required_documents: NOTHING CAN BE SUBMITTED FOR 2026/27 - the application portal offers no Wood Technology application. Historical list for the final 2025/26 intake: (a) an account on the Application Portal (https://aws.unibz.it/exup) plus a valid ID card or passport scanned front and back - 'if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure'; (b) the completed online form with all attachments; (c) for candidates with a foreign qualification, the diploma - 'if you are not yet in possession of the diploma, you'll need to upload it upon enrolment'; (d) language evidence - a self-declaration where the certificate was awarded by an Italian public institution, a scanned copy of the original where awarded by a foreign public institution, plus a school or university letter stating the medium of instruction where the diploma does not show it; (e) for parity-of-treatment applicants, a copy of the valid Italian permit to stay, or a renewal request if expired. NO structured study-career Excel template was required (that upload belongs to master applications), and NO school report cards or self-certified grades were required either - unlike the Bachelor in Sustainable Agriculture and Forestry, this programme scored candidates by examination rather than by school record, so the document burden was unusually light. At enrolment, holders of a foreign secondary school qualification additionally had to upload the diploma, an official Italian translation (not required for diplomas issued in German or English), and the applicable ARDI/CIMEA statements (see credential_recognition). Standard warning: 'Mendacious declarations will be criminally prosecuted and will result in the automatic exclusion from the ranking list.'
application_fee: NO FEE IS PAYABLE FOR 2026/27 because no application can be made. Historically the standard unibz rule applied: EUR 50, charged only to non-EU citizens living abroad - 'Application fee: EUR 50. The fee is an administration fee and is non-refundable.' EU citizens and persons given parity of treatment, including non-EU nationals holding an Italian work, family, humanitarian, asylum or religious residence permit, paid no application fee.
tuition_or_fees_link: Approximately EUR 1,200 per academic year in two instalments, per the detailed fee section published for the final 2025/26 intake: 'Fees amount to EUR 1200. 1st instalment (EUR 600): includes the revenue stamp of EUR 16. 2nd instalment (EUR 600): must be paid by March of the following year.' CAUTION - unibz's own current materials contradict each other on the headline figure: the English programme page and the English brochure both state 'Studiengebühren: ca. 1200 EUR pro Jahr', while the German page, the Italian page and the Italian brochure all state approximately EUR 1,350 per year ('Tasse di iscrizione: ca. 1350 EUR per anno'). The EUR 1,350 figure closely matches the EUR 1,347.50 charged under the 2019/20 L-9 predecessor programme, which suggests it is a stale carry-over that the Italian and German pages never updated, and that EUR 1,200 - matching the detailed instalment breakdown and the fee level at other unibz bachelors - is the correct recent figure. Standard conditions: 'Delayed payment of the second instalment will result in a fine being levied. If you have not paid the tuition fees, you will be unable to take exams and will not be able to transfer to other universities or other study programmes.' No refund on drop-out, interruption or exclusion. Exemptions: students with a disability recognised under article 3, paragraph 1 of Law No 104/1992 or with a disability of 66% or more (certificate to be handed in at the start of the academic year), and foreign students granted a scholarship from the Italian government; holders of a scholarship from the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano receive a refund of the fees. Fee pages: https://guide.unibz.it/en/study-career/general-information/fees and https://www.unibz.it/en/applicants/studying-at-unibz . For 2026/27 these fees are payable only by continuing students in the teach-out, not by any new entrant. [uncertain]
scholarships_grants: No scholarship specific to Wood Technology was ever published, and for 2026/27 the question is academic for new applicants since none can enrol; the general provincial regime remains relevant to students in the teach-out. Main instrument: the study grant of the Autonomous Province of South Tyrol, administered by the Ufficio per il diritto allo studio universitario / Amt fuer Hochschulfoerderung and awarded on income and merit, quoted by unibz at between EUR 1,680 and EUR 6,960 per year, with grant holders additionally receiving a refund of tuition fees. Three provincial instruments exist - ordinary study grants, merit scholarships, and grants fostering postgraduate studies - applied for through the provincial e-government service. Merit route: students who after the first year achieve an average grade of 27/30 may apply for merit-based rather than income-based scholarships. Decisive restriction for international students: non-EU students can apply for a provincial study grant only if they hold a long-term residence permit or have been resident in South Tyrol for at least one uninterrupted year, so a first-year non-EU student arriving on a study visa was effectively excluded in year one. Foreign students and Italian students living abroad may also apply for scholarships funded by the Ministero degli Affari Esteri. One programme-specific financial feature is worth noting in place of a scholarship: the compulsory 50 ECTS of in-company placement, backed by agreements with the Consiglio Nazionale dei Periti Industriali, the Collegio dei Periti Industriali of the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano and companies of the South Tyrol Business Federation (Unternehmerverband Suedtirol / Assoimprenditori Alto Adige), which in practice gave students paid or subsidised industry time - but this is an internship arrangement, not a grant. The figures above are drawn from unibz's general applicant pages and were not re-verified against a programme-specific source in this check. [uncertain]
credential_recognition: The standard unibz foreign-qualification regime applied while the programme recruited; it is now relevant only to students already enrolled. At enrolment, holders of a foreign secondary school qualification had to upload the diploma plus an official translation into Italian ('not necessary for diplomas issued in German or English'), and then, depending on the education system: (a) EU countries, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, International Baccalaureate, European Baccalaureate - the Statement of Correspondence from ARDI, the Automatic Recognition Database Italy (https://ardi.cimea.it/en); (b) non-EU countries that are signatories to the Lisbon Convention - the ARDI Statement of Correspondence AND the CIMEA Statement of Verification; (c) non-EU countries that are not signatories of the Lisbon Convention - the CIMEA Statement of Comparability AND the CIMEA Statement of Verification (https://cimea-diplome.it/). Turkey is a signatory of the Lisbon Recognition Convention, so a Turkish applicant fell into category (b): ARDI Statement of Correspondence plus CIMEA Statement of Verification, with an official Italian translation of the Turkish-language diploma. 'unibz performs the necessary checks on your foreign qualification and in case of doubt reserves the right to request additional documents', and 'if you do not possess a valid admission qualification, you can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment.' The 180-ECTS evidence requirement mentioned in the field definition applies to master admission, not to this bachelor. Separately, and now the more useful provision: credit from previous study can be carried into another programme - 'Credit points from previous university studies can only be recognised after enrolment if the exams taken at the university of provenance are equivalent in content to those offered at unibz' - and unibz explicitly promises favourable treatment to Wood Technology students moving to Industrial and Mechanical Engineering (see uncertainty_notes).
non_eu_visa_process: NO VISA PATHWAY EXISTS FOR THIS PROGRAMME IN 2026/27: with no admission round there is no ranking list, no first instalment to pay and therefore no Universitaly pre-enrolment, and a non-EU applicant cannot obtain a study visa on the basis of this degree. Historical sequence while the programme recruited: apply in the single Early Bird window with the EUR 50 fee; if admitted, secure the place by paying the first instalment; then 'start your visa application on the Universitaly portal. The application on Universitaly is mandatory, otherwise you will not be allowed to enrol. On Universitaly you can apply for one study programme only.' The Italian diplomatic-consular representation then issued the study visa - 'Once you are eligible for admission (check the ranking lists) and have also applied on Universitaly, the Italian Authorities in your own country will issue you the entry visa for studies/university.' Proof of financial means under the general unibz guidance: at least EUR 800 per month for living costs excluding tuition, which unibz translates into at least EUR 36,000 for a bachelor programme (EUR 24,000 for a master), plus health insurance, visa expenses and the annual tuition. After arrival: 'According to Italian law, within 8 working days of your arrival in Italy, you must have applied for the residence permit: as soon as you arrive, get in touch with the Advisory Service', and the permesso di soggiorno must then be handed to the Student Office in person or by e-mail. Work while studying is capped at 20 hours per week and 1,040 hours per year. Refund exception: non-EU applicants abroad who could not obtain the enrolment documents from the Italian authorities were entitled to a refund of the instalment paid. IMPORTANT CAVEAT specific to this programme: only 2 non-EU places existed per cycle, and because no ranking list for Wood Technology could be located in the public archive, there is no evidence that the non-EU route ever produced an admission here.

THE FILE IS AN EMPTY SHELL AND THIS IS A KEY FINDING. Verified by direct download and text extraction on 2026-08-29: the English PDF is 55 KB and its complete extractable text consists only of 'Subject to change. Latest update: 21.05.2026', the Advisory Service address block (Universitaetsplatz 1 / piazza Universita 1, 39100 Bozen-Bolzano, +39 0471 012100, apply@unibz.it), opening hours, and the TCPDF generator line. There are no deadlines, no available places, no entry requirements, no language requirements, no selection procedure, no fees. The German version is identical in this respect. For every ACTIVE unibz programme this same PDF path returns a 9-page document that is the richest single source of admission data, so the emptiness here is a direct machine-readable signal of suspension - and a trap for any pipeline that treats HTTP 200 on this path as proof that a programme is recruiting.

uncertainty_notes: 1) HEADLINE, AND THE POINT OF THIS RECORD: the programme is NOT available for 2026/27 and must be surfaced to users as unavailable. The suspension is stated by unibz in all three languages and corroborated by five independent signals (stripped admission section, empty admission PDF in EN and DE, absence from every 2026/27 ranking list, absence from the Additional Application Session, and a 2026/27 course offering containing no first-year subjects). Confidence: very high. 2) SUSPENSION IS NOT CLOSURE: teaching continues for enrolled students, with 19 second- and third-year course units scheduled for 2026/27 and a 2027/28 tab already present (currently empty). The correct label is 'no new intake / teach-out', not 'abolished'. 3) WHETHER IT RETURNS IS UNKNOWN. unibz's wording is year-specific ('will not be offered in the 2026/27 academic year') and does not say the programme is discontinued permanently. No decree, news item or press release announcing or explaining the suspension was found in English, German or Italian, and no reactivation date is published. Do not present the suspension as either temporary or permanent - present it as 'not offered in 2026/27, future status unannounced'. 4) LAST INTAKE was 2025/26, established by comparing archived versions of the programme page: the March 2025 snapshot carries a complete admission section with 2025 deadlines, places and an admission exam on 2025-05-14, and the April 2024 snapshot the equivalent for 2024/25. 5) SCRAPER TRAPS, several and severe: the programme is still listed in the Engineering faculty navigation among active bachelors; the live page still shows the stale recruitment string 'Courses will definetely be starting'; both brochure PDFs still return HTTP 200 with full content advertising 20 EU + 2 non-EU places; and the admission-information PDF also returns HTTP 200 despite being empty. Any pipeline keying on menu presence, PDF existence or HTTP status will misclassify this programme as open. The reliable machine-readable signals are the empty admission PDF, the absent 'Application and Admission' section, and absence from the ranking-list index. 6) TUITION CONFLICT, unresolved in unibz's own materials: EN page and EN brochure say approximately EUR 1,200/year; DE page, IT page and IT brochure say approximately EUR 1,350/year, for the same programme and the same brochure edition. The archived detailed fee section supports EUR 1,200 (600 + 600), and EUR 1,350 closely matches the EUR 1,347.50 of the 2019/20 L-9 predecessor, so EUR 1,350 is most likely a stale carry-over - but unibz has not corrected it. 7) BROCHURE IS STALE: title page '2024/25', footer 'Latest update: 21.05.2026', and in the English edition the whole Kurzinfo box is untranslated German. It describes a curriculum no longer recruiting. 8) NO RANKING LIST SURVIVES from any cycle, so there is no admitted-score floor, no applicant count and no exclusion count - competitiveness and the real accessibility of the 2 non-EU places cannot be quantified, unlike sister bachelors where signed decrees do quantify them. 9) SELECTION RUBRIC only ever published as a single figure ('max. 100 points' in 2025/26, 'max. 60 points' in 2024/25); no component breakdown, no pass mark, no cut-off and no tie-break rule were published, and the OFA 'inadequate prior knowledge' threshold is not quantified. 10) DEGREE-CLASS AND NAME HISTORY is reconstructed, not documented in one place: L-9 'Ingegneria del Legno' in 2019/20 to L-P03 'Tecnologie del Legno / Holztechnik / Wood Technology' at an unstated later date, with three curricula consolidated into two majors and State-Examination-free register access introduced.
